newsitem.title: UK: Reed shares still hungover from downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Reed shares still hungover from downgrades.

text.p: Reed International Plc's shares on Tuesday continued to suffer from the hangover induced by last week's profit downgrades stemming from concern about the impact of a strong pound on group profits.

Reed was down to a low of 1,063 pence earlier but has since recovered alightly to 1,071, down 12 pence per share. One market maker said there was no fresh factor impacting on the shares, explaining: "There must still be stock going around the market."
As Reed remains sluggish, sterling continues its run of strength. It gained one pfennig against the German mark and half a cent against the dollar in early European trade.

Sterling was one of the factors cited by analysts for the profit downgrades last week which knocked the shares lower. Reed has shown a volatile performance this year, plunging from a year high of 1,207 pence per share.
Currency pain looks unlikely to abate with the pound remaining buoyant and shrugging off political turmoil surrounding Europe after a good performance in Asian trading overnight.
